panels.rationale: Clinical photograph of a human patient showing a flesh-colored cutaneous nodule on the hand of a 37-year-old male, which is directly attributed to fibroblastic rheumatism in the caption and title.
panels.attribution_text: Suri et al. Firm Cutaneous Nodule on the Dorsal Hand: A Case Report on Fibroblastic Rheumatism.. Cureus 2020. doi:10.7759/cureus.10312. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Clinical presentation of a fibroblastic rheumatism nodule on the hand of a 37-year-old Caucasian male The lesion, outlined in purple ink, consists of a 0.8 x 0.6-cm firm, flesh-colored cutaneous nodule on the index finger of the left dorsal hand
in_text_mentions: Physical exam revealed a single 0.8 x 0.6-cm indurated, flesh-colored to pink nodule on the dorsal surface of the patient’s left hand, just distal to the second metacarpophalangeal joint (Figure 1). The remainder of the patient’s physical exam and review of systems were negative.
